Checking back against example 1, the three 2s at top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right do correspond to rays in exactly those three directions, and example 2's lone top-left 2 produces a single up-left ray — so this direction-toward-the-2s rule holds consistently across cases so far.

Rows 6-7 confirmed. Now checking example 1's square with three diagonal directions - tracing each expansion (up-right, down-left, down-right) row by row to confirm the resulting shape matches the expected union of cells.
